common_name: Daylily 'Baby Boomer' (Yellow with Purple Eyezone, Early-Season Diploid)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; this compact diploid daylily carries yellow flowers marked with a purple eyezone above a green throat on 24-inch scapes.

directions: Registered by Tim Herrington in 1996 from a cross of a seedling crossed with Rocky's Eye, then crossed again with Daggy, Baby Boomer is a diploid daylily with evergreen foliage bearing yellow flowers about 3.5 inches across marked with a purple eyezone above a green throat, carried on 24-inch scapes that open in the early season. It later became a parent, crossed with Green Rainbow, of Tim Herrington's 2006 introduction One Eye Willie. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Daylily 'Jungle Mask' (Cream-Pink with Royal Purple Eyezone)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid daylily bears cream-pink flowers edged with a royal purple eyezone on 28-inch scapes.

directions: Registered by E.H. Salter in 1990, Jungle Mask is a tetraploid daylily with evergreen foliage bearing cream-pink flowers about six inches across, edged with a royal purple eyezone above a green throat, carried on 28-inch scapes that open in midseason with rebloom. It later became one of the two parents, crossed with Well of Souls, of Salter's own 1991 introduction Pirate's Patch, winner of the American Hemerocallis Society's Don C. Stevens Award. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Daylily 'Well of Souls' (Peach-Pink and Lavender Blend with Black-Purple Eyezone)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; this tetraploid daylily bears a peach-pink and lavender blend flower with a black-purple eyezone on 26-inch scapes.

directions: Registered by E.H. Salter in 1988, Well of Souls is a tetraploid daylily with semi-evergreen foliage bearing a peach-pink and lavender blend flower about six inches across, marked with a black-purple eyezone above a green throat, carried on 26-inch scapes that open in midseason with rebloom. It later became one of the two parents, crossed with Jungle Mask, of Salter's own 1991 introduction Pirate's Patch, winner of the American Hemerocallis Society's Don C. Stevens Award. Plant divisions in average, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing congested clumps every three to four years to maintain vigorous flowering.
